tasks.task: Write the investor story and slide-by-slide deck text

items.when: When you have the founder's model, metrics and notes and need the story and text for each slide
When the idea is still fuzzy, to answer six sharp questions before any slide is written
Before you fix the slide order, to try a different arc that builds belief step by step
When the deck is drafted, to back every claim with a dated source in an appendix
Before the deck goes out, to find numbers that do not match from slide to slide
When the text is agreed and the founder wants a first laid-out deck fast
When the deck lists facts and never moves from how things are to how they could be

tasks.task: Review a deck against the questions investors ask

items.when: When investors keep asking the same questions or said they did not get it
Before meetings start, to have tough investors grill the pitch and vote in or out
When the deck runs long, to test slide count, talk time and type size
When you want the market, traction, money and team read as an investor would
After each no, to rank the doubts heard and revise the pitch against them

tasks.task: Cut a short teaser from the full deck

items.when: When a full deck exists and first contact needs five slides, with what to hold back
When the opening line is weak, to compare 10, 30 and 60 second versions
Before sending, to check the teaser's numbers still match the full deck
Before the teaser is sent, to check each number and logo on it against the full deck's sources

tasks.task: Write the spoken pitch and prepare for questions

items.when: When the founder must speak the pitch in one, three or ten minutes
When the pitch is new, to draft a short honest version and improve it after each meeting
When you need the toughest objections found and an answer tied to evidence for each
Before the first meeting, to rehearse against a panel that pushes back
When the pitch sounds impressive but cannot be said plainly in two sentences

tasks.task: Plan the round from decision to close

items.when: When the founder decides to raise, or runway is shorter than a raise usually takes
Before setting dates, to know the month cash runs out at current burn
When the round size must come from a model with a cash-out date and ranges
When the founder needs a value range to set expectations before talking terms
Before the round plan is fixed, to compare two plans that use the runway and the founder's time differently

tasks.task: Build or check the financial model behind the raise

items.when: When the raise needs a three to five year model with revenue, costs, cash and scenarios
When the model is built, to find which bets break first and what to test
Before an investor opens the workbook, to catch formula errors and broken links
When the founder built the model alone, to have figures recalculated and cases tested

tasks.task: Size the market and map the competition for the deck

items.when: When the market slide needs a bottom-up number with facts and guesses told apart
When you want the size cross-checked top-down and bottom-up
When the competition slide needs rivals compared from sourced facts
When the deck claims a huge market and cannot name the small one it will own first

tasks.task: Turn raw numbers into traction investors can check

items.when: When you have revenue and customer data and need recurring revenue, churn and payback read
When investors will ask for cohorts, lifetime value against acquisition cost, and payback
When retention is the proof and needs curves by sign-up group
When a number could be worked out two ways, to fix one definition before it is quoted

tasks.task: Set investor fit criteria and score the investor list

items.when: When the founder has an investor list and needs it scored on stage, cheque, sector and place
When facts on one investor are thin, to build a sourced file before scoring them

tasks.task: Write outreach notes for the top investors

items.when: Before writing to anyone, to know why each investor fits and what to lead with
When a note must cite what the investor has backed or said, with sources
When each note must sound like the founder, to get versions tied to a real detail
Before sending, to test each claim in the note and the basics of the message

tasks.task: Write a forwardable intro email for a contact

items.when: When a contact has offered an intro and needs a short email they can forward
When the one-line description is weak, to compare a few short versions first
Before handing it over, to score the email and cut what an investor will skip

tasks.task: Keep the fundraising pipeline and follow-ups

items.when: When meetings start and the plan's stages must become a tracker
After calls and emails, to update each investor's status and follow-up
When promises to investors pile up and due follow-ups need drafting each week

tasks.task: Build a clean cap table from the share records

items.when: When you have the share register, grants, SAFEs and notes and must list conflicts first
When SAFEs sit on the table, to check what each owns before and after a priced round
Before founders rely on it, to check formulas and that ownership adds to 100 percent

tasks.task: Model the next round and check each conversion

items.when: When the table is clean and you need ownership before and after the round
When a SAFE converts in a priced round with an option pool top-up
When a note converts and interest, cap and discount decide the share count
When an instrument converts at the lower of cap or discount and both must be shown
When investors ask for a bigger option pool before they invest
When round terms keep changing and the SAFE result must be reworked each time

tasks.task: Compare round options side by side

items.when: When the founder weighs sizes, valuations or instruments and needs each shown in ownership
When each option needs a defensible value range behind it
When a startup loan is one option and its cost, warrants and covenants need explaining
When one option is a lower-priced round and earlier investors' rights change

tasks.task: Turn a term sheet into numbers and lawyer questions

items.when: When one or more term sheets arrive and the founder needs ownership and sale outcomes in numbers
When you need the risky terms flagged in plain words and when to call the lawyer
When preference terms differ, to see what investors and founders each get at a sale
When the sheet has price protection and its effect in a later lower round must be shown
When only one sheet is on the table and the founder still needs to push on terms
When the founder is about to accept the first terms to avoid a hard talk

tasks.task: Build the data room index for the round

items.when: When an investor asks for documents, or before term sheets so the round does not stall
When files exist and need a versioned index and a map of what requests they cover
Before filling the room, to know what an investor's checks will ask for
When the room is filled, to read it as an investor and find what is missing

tasks.task: Write the monthly investor update

items.when: When the month's numbers close and the update is due on its fixed date
When you have the KPI sheet, P&L and notes and need a short, honest update with asks
When the story could be framed more than one way, to get a second version to compare
When the month went badly and the loss, the numbers and the plan must be said straight
Before sending, to find where the update contradicts the deck or the last update
Before the update goes out, to trace every metric, date and customer name to the company's own records

tasks.task: Write a quarterly letter with a clear story

items.when: When three monthly updates need pulling into one quarterly letter
When the numbers could tell more than one story, to draft the point, proof and next step
When the letter covers a full year and needs principles, a cash check and mistakes owned
Before it goes out, to check the letter matches what the board and team were told
When the letter hides a mistake that the investors will find anyway

tasks.task: Prepare for a board or investor meeting

items.when: When a board meeting or investor call is coming and tough questions need honest answers
When the update is drafted, to drill the numbers and own the weak spots
When the meeting needs a deck with the story, numbers and bad news placed right
When the board must decide something and needs an evidence map
When last quarter's deck is reused, to update every number and list what changed

tasks.task: Explain ownership to founders and team in plain words

items.when: When founders and team need who owns what before and after the round in plain numbers
When new hires will get equity and grant sizes need a model
Before the team reads it, to find cap table jargon and put it in plain words

always.when: Before anything goes to an investor, to find every claim that has no number or source
When deck, update and data room exist together, to check they tell one story

helpers.when: When the deck text is final and the slides need designing
When the raise needs a driver-based model built or rebuilt
When the market size and competition need proper sourced research
When the positioning is unclear and the deck cannot say who the product is for
When the round involves debt, a lender or wider finance decisions
When the founder chooses to raise from the crowd as well as investors

gaps: No library item sets investor fit criteria or scores an investor list; only the kit skill does
No library item finds investors by stage, sector, cheque size and place; the research item covers one named firm at a time
No library item keeps a fundraising pipeline tracker with stage, next step and last contact for each investor
No library item builds a whole cap table from share records; library items each check one conversion or one pool
No library item lays out round options side by side: priced round, SAFE or note, at different sizes and values
No library item plans a round: how much to raise, milestones the money buys, use of funds and a timeline
No library item writes a routine monthly investor update; the library covers bad news and board stories only
No library item cuts a teaser deck or writes a one-page investor summary for a startup
No library item builds a data room index for a venture round; the document index was written for company sales
No library item compares whole term sheets on control terms such as board seats, vetoes and pro rata rights
No library item explains options, vesting and dilution to staff, or helps founders split equity
No library item covers accelerator applications, equity crowdfunding rounds or non-dilutive startup grants
No library item writes a forwardable intro or a thank-you and follow-up after an investor meeting
